# Real frames from the screen recording

These three GIFs use actual frames from my recovered screen recording. They are chronological extracts, with readable crops and labels outside the recorded image. The first zooms in on Grok becoming active again; the other two show my recorded navigation between chats.

1. **Grok starts again** — source +409–416 seconds. The zoom is added for reading. The +411.7–412.2 transition is shown five times slower; the rest plays at normal speed.
2. **Back and forth between chats** — source +269–303 seconds, played at twice the source-file speed.
3. **Reviewer → Grok → reviewer** — source +331–349 seconds, played at twice the source-file speed.

Each GIF loops directly from its last recorded frame back to its first, without title slides or an end card. Repeated playback is not evidence of another recorded event. No frames are played backward. No click indicators have been added.

The recording was reconstructed with an assumed frame rate of 30 fps. The labels give positions in that file; they do not establish exact original wall-clock timing. The frames show activity restarting and my navigation. They do not establish the restart trigger, automatic redirection, or deliberate control of my mouse.

`manifest.json` contains the source SHA-256, each GIF hash, and the source frame index, crop, timing, and playback factor for every recorded frame. No editorial slides are inserted. `source-recording.mp4` is an unchanged evidence copy. The before/after pixels in the restart extract match the earlier preserved frames.
